page: Amazon Web Services c7i.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs derived from 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, passmark CPU scores, and memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached read operations. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, which contribute to top-tier results in ray tracing, image processing, and cryptographic operations. Single-core performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the average to strong categories, indicating that workloads must be highly parallelized to fully exploit the hardware.

The lack of local NVMe storage means all storage operations rely on network-attached volumes, which may introduce latency compared to local-storage instances. However, the high memory bandwidth and 50 Gbps network baseline support data-intensive tasks. The instance demonstrates strong performance in LLM inference for medium and large models, static web serving, and database operations. This profile makes it suitable for high-compute workloads such as software compilation, cryptography, web serving, and parallelized scientific simulations.
